title: Results from Semiconductor Supply Chain Request for Information
book_use: Chapter 1: more than 150 responses; median inventory for hardest-to-get chips fell from about 40 days in 2019 to less than 5 days in 2021; use to frame inventory as stored time and distinguish product-specific bottlenecks.

title: 2026 State of the U.S. Semiconductor Industry
book_use: Chapters 1-2 and current context: U.S.-headquartered companies' 2025 global sales share and announced U.S. private-sector semiconductor ecosystem investment since 2020; label investment as announced rather than completed.

title: 2025 State of the U.S. Semiconductor Industry
book_use: Background: long-run decline in U.S. manufacturing share and CHIPS-era investment context; distinguish manufacturing share from design and revenue leadership.

title: TSMC Arizona
book_use: Chapter 2 and later Arizona chapter: first Arizona fab entered N4 high-volume production in Q4 2024; later fab and packaging timelines; distinguish producing from planned capacity.

title: Annual Report 2025
book_use: Chapters 2 and 5: ASML describes itself as the world's only EUV lithography-system manufacturer and identifies Carl Zeiss SMT as sole supplier of critical optics; use as recursive concentration case.

title: CHIPS Incentives Awards for Corning, Edwards Vacuum, and Infinera
book_use: Chapter 2: illustrates semiconductor ecosystem inputs beyond fabs, including dry vacuum pumps used beneath manufacturing facilities; award size is not a proxy for strategic importance.

title: Gallium Statistics and Information
book_use: Chapters 2 and 7: U.S. dependence on imported primary gallium and semiconductor uses of gallium compounds; distinguish low-purity primary material from higher-purity processing and downstream wafers.

author_or_institution: National Institute of Standards and Technology
title: National Advanced Packaging Manufacturing Program
book_use: Chapters 2, 3, and 9: advanced packaging is treated as a first-order capability for high-performance computing and AI; program objective is a self-sustaining high-volume domestic packaging industry.

title: Commerce Finalizes $1.4 Billion in CHIPS Awards for Advanced Packaging
book_use: Chapter 3 and later packaging chapter: substrates, materials, and packaging R&D receive dedicated CHIPS funding; supports the claim that strategic attention has moved beyond wafer fabs.

author_or_institution: National Institute of Standards and Technology
title: Department of Commerce Announces Letters of Intent for 7 Companies for $874 Million in CHIPS R&D Awards
book_use: Chapters 3, 8, 9, and 19: current R&D priorities include memory, advanced packaging, substrates, materials, photonics, and provenance.

title: HBM4 Validation Enters Crucial Stage
book_use: Chapters 3 and 8: Samsung, SK hynix, and Micron are the three major HBM suppliers competing through HBM4 validation; use as current market-structure context, not as an immutable share forecast.

title: Defense Industrial Base: Actions Needed to Improve Visibility and Coordination
book_use: Chapter 3 and traceability chapters: DOD relies on a global network of more than 200,000 suppliers and has limited insight into portions of the network; use as an analogy for multi-tier dependency visibility.

title: Critical Minerals: Actions Needed to Address Risks to Semiconductor and Battery Supply Chains
book_use: Chapters 4 and 7: substitution and recycling may not reduce short-term semiconductor import reliance; supports separating long-run technical substitutes from executable emergency substitutes.

title: Ohio One Construction Timeline Update
book_use: Chapter 4 and later cost/infrastructure chapters: revised Ohio fab construction and operations timelines illustrate why leading-edge capacity cannot be created on emergency timescales.

title: Semiconductor Manufacturing: Commerce Has Made Progress but Needs Plans for Research and Development Programs
book_use: Chapter 4 and implementation chapters: funded-project counts, disbursement progress, milestone execution, and stalled R&D elements; use to avoid both 'CHIPS solved it' and 'CHIPS did nothing' narratives.

title: Adjusting Imports of Semiconductors, Semiconductor Manufacturing Equipment, and Their Derivative Products into the United States
book_use: Opening context: executive-branch Section 232 finding that the U.S. consumes roughly a quarter of world semiconductors and fully manufactures about 10% of chips it requires; attribute as a government finding and retain the date.

author_or_institution: National Institute of Standards and Technology
title: Semiconductor Traceability and Provenance Workshop
book_use: Chapter 19: counterfeit risk, malicious tampering, opaque sourcing, provenance, and traceability as semiconductor supply-chain security concerns.

title: Commerce Department Announces Industrial Base Survey of American Semiconductor Supply Chain
book_use: Chapter 10: mature-node/current-generation semiconductors remain important to automotive, telecommunications, medical, defense, and other critical sectors.

title: Chipping Away: Assessing and Addressing the Labor Market Gap Facing the U.S. Semiconductor Industry
book_use: Chapter 12: projected U.S. semiconductor workforce expansion and possible technical-worker shortfall by 2030; present as a projection with assumptions, not a fact already realized.

author_or_institution: U.S. Bureau of Industry and Security
title: Department of Commerce Revises License Review Policy for Semiconductors Exported to China
book_use: Chapter 17: current case-by-case licensing policy for specified advanced accelerators; date all export-control rules because they change quickly.

author_or_institution: U.S. Bureau of Industry and Security
title: Department of Commerce Closes Export Controls Loophole for Foreign-Owned Semiconductor Fabs in China
book_use: Chapter 17: illustrates policy changes affecting foreign-owned fabs and the importance of second-order operational effects of controls.

title: Samsung Austin Semiconductor — Taylor
book_use: Chapters 11-15: current Texas fab investment and operating timeline context; distinguish investment plans from realized qualified output.
